spec_match.rationale: Probes navigator.mcpServer — a surface that exists in no spec or Chromium build — and frames WebMCP as a JSON-RPC MCP server endpoint; the spec has no tools/call JSON-RPC exchange in the page, it uses document.modelContext.executeTool().

interactive.rationale: Tool list (click and Enter/Space), generated parameter forms, Invoke, and Clear all work and produce request/response trace entries, but everything is a local mock with random outputs.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index blurb says the page invokes tools from a 'simulated MCP server registry', which is accurate, but it is a generic MCP JSON-RPC demo rather than WebMCP.

edge_cases.rationale: Required parameters are not enforced (Invoke with empty query sends only {limit:5}, isError:false); there is no error/isError path except calc parse errors. The stale-selection race was fixed 2026-11-08 (invocation snapshots the invoked tool).

references.rationale: See-also section added 2026-11-08 with chromestatus.com/feature/5117755740913664 (invariant #3), sibling concepts and modelcontextprotocol.io; no WebMCP spec/explainer link yet.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite (6 assertions) reports 6/6 PASS on CfT 153 both with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features; without the flag every assertion passes vacuously (guards like !('modelContext' in document)||…), and registertool-rejects-tool-without-name passes only because reading registerTool off undefined throws TypeError — a false pass that needs a human to review (suite is immutable). The suite targets document.modelContext while this page probes navigator.modelContext.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 driven by Node Playwright (chromium.launch) against a local server on :3111 — NOT chrome-devtools-mcp, which is unavailable in this environment, so this is not DevTools-MCP-verified evidence; no accessibility-tree dump was taken. Bugs reproduced: (1) the placeholder trace line is never removed (selector pre[style*="555"] never matches); (2) invoking search_documents then clicking get_weather inside the 300–700ms delay returns a get_weather result under request id 2; (3) location '' executes (window.__xss===1) via highlightJSON→innerHTML. Badge says navigator.mcpServer unavailable, with and without the flag. UPDATE 2026-11-08: all three bugs fixed — Fix verified on headless Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 via Node Playwright (not chrome-devtools-mcp) on local :3112, 360x740 DPR3 touch + 1280x800; screenshots in /tmp/claude-0/shots/webmcp-fix/. (1) placeholder removed on first trace entry and again after Clear; (2) invoke search_documents then select get_weather mid-delay → response id 2 carries search_documents results; (3) XSS payload renders as literal text, window.__xss undefined. All four tools invoked, keyboard Enter select, Clear work; zero console errors/failed requests; 0px overflow both classes.

telemetry_health.rationale: Only shared runtime/console capture; it recorded the 'Invalid or unexpected token' pageerror from the injected handler.

design_system.rationale: Variables and paired button colours; readable in screenshot.

accessibility.rationale: Tool rows are role=button with tabindex and key handlers, but parameter <label>s are not associated (no for=), the selected tool has no aria-pressed/selected, and the trace has no live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px overflow both classes; one control under 44px on mobile.

openQuestions.title: Remove the fictional navigator.mcpServer probe and reframe on document.modelContext
openQuestions.detail: navigator.mcpServer does not exist; the real flagged surface on CfT 153 is document.modelContext (registerTool/getTools/executeTool). Register the four tools there when present, call executeTool(tool, JSON.stringify(args)), and label the JSON-RPC panel as an MCP-protocol analogy, not WebMCP wire format. Give exact flag steps (chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features).

openQuestions.title: Enforce required params, associate labels, add the WebMCP spec link
openQuestions.detail: Placeholder removal was fixed 2026-11-08 (.trace-placeholder class). Still open: required inputs (*) should block or return an isError result; add for= to generated labels; the see-also now links ChromeStatus but not the WebMCP spec (webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp).

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Never interpolate user-controlled strings into innerHTML; use textContent or DOM construction.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Followed (fixed 2026-11-08) — highlightJSON builds text nodes + spans via textContent; trace labels use textContent.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce asynchronous/changing results through a polite live region (role=status/log or aria-live) and keep controls as native buttons with accessible names.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Not followed — trace has no live region.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic/grid layouts that collapse to one column at narrow widths (minmax(0,1fr), container/media queries) so no fixed-column track forces horizontal overflow.

guidanceConsulted.query: prevent DOM XSS when rendering user input textContent trusted types
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: If you only need plain text, prefer element.textContent (not a Trusted Types sink) over innerHTML; never interpolate untrusted strings into HTML templates.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied — the JSON trace highlighter tokenises JSON.stringify output and appends span/text nodes; location renders literally, window.__xss undefined.

summary: A generic MCP JSON-RPC playground mislabelled as WebMCP, probing a non-existent navigator.mcpServer, with no ChromeStatus link and three reproducible bugs: an XSS sink, a stale-selection race, and a placeholder that never clears. 2026-11-08 fix: XSS sink, stale-selection race and stuck placeholder fixed, and a ChromeStatus see-also added; the navigator.mcpServer reframe remains open.
